svg.text: United Airlines Dispatch & Weight-and-Balance Outage Architecture
Pilot application disruption and pre-takeoff manifest requirements (Nov 16, 2026)

g.text: 1. Dispatch Outage
Hypothesis
Web-Based Operations Ingress
United central flight operations relies on web APIs
to bridge gate passenger manifests and flight planning.
Internal IT outage stalled pilot application access
to takeoff calculation and manifest data.
Worker-level behavior was not publicly disclosed.
Hypothetical Calculation Stall
Model: Communication hang between gateway proxies
and weight-and-balance engine leaves queues empty.
EFB request sessions timed out without response.
Automated dispatch releases could not be generated.
System stalled across all domestic mainline hubs.
Pilot Electronic Flight Bag Hang
The precise application message was not disclosed.
Captains could not review passenger load numbers.
Takeoff flap and stabilizer trim settings missing.
Crews held aircraft at boarding gates nationwide.
Internal IT problem confirmed; zero FAA or ATC fault.
2. Gate Ground Holds
Safety
14 CFR § 121.665 Compliance
Manifest must be prepared and signed by
authorized personnel before each takeoff.
Incorrect center of gravity risks aerodynamic stall.
Some crews waited at gates for flight information.
Mainline aircraft held at gates until release.
90+ Minute Departure Cascades
Delays exceeded 90 to 100 minutes at major hubs.
O'Hare, Newark, Houston, Denver gates gridlocked.
About 600 United flights were delayed that evening.
The share caused by this outage was unclear.
Operational delays can affect crew schedules.
Airborne & Express Safe
Airborne flights held certified manifests and landed.
United Express regional flights operated normally.
Zero airborne safety or flight control risks occurred.
United reported an internal technology problem.
Flights already airborne and Express were unaffected.
3. System Recovery
Resolution
Dispatch Application Recovery
United initiated recovery across dispatch tiers.
Pre-flight calculation services re-initialized.
Gateway communication channels cleared and reset.
Aerodynamic calculation queues resume processing.
Flight data connections resynced across airport hubs.
Cockpit Manifest Downloads
Flight crews retrieve certified load manifests.
Manifest signing completed per 14 CFR § 121.665.
Takeoff trim and V-speeds loaded into flight computers.
ATC begins departure release sequencing.
Ground holds gradually lifted at major hubs.
Operational Normalization
United confirmed complete system resolution.
Zero cyberattack or external breach detected.
Safety doctrine prevented any uncertified takeoffs.
Mainline operations normalized through the night.
Highlighted need for client-side offline EFB engines.
4. Engineering Safeguards & Aviation Dispatch Architecture
Client-Side Offline Calculation Engines
1. Local EFB Aerodynamic Engines: Embed verified weight-and-balance logic
directly in iOS/iPadOS EFB apps to calculate trim without backend APIs.
2. Gate-to-Cockpit Direct Sync: Support direct peer-to-peer Bluetooth/LAN
manifest transfer between gate agent scanners and cockpit tablets.
3. Automated Socket Health Watchdogs: Kill deadlocked gateway child
processes automatically when socket write timeouts exceed 5 seconds.
4. Hot-Standby Dispatch Enclaves: Maintain parallel, independent dispatch
clusters with active-active traffic routing to eliminate single-point hangs.
Guarantees aircraft departure clearance even during cloud gateway stalls.
Departure Recovery & Queue Management
1. Priority EDCT Scheduling: During post-outage recovery, prioritize flights
with narrow departure slot windows or crew duty expiration thresholds.
2. Staggered Pushback Waves: Coordinate hub pushbacks in 10-minute waves
to prevent taxiway gridlock and aircraft engine fuel-burn waste.
3. Automated Crew Leg Legality Checks: Run async crew-timeout simulations
to proactively reassign reserve pilots before duty limits expire at gates.
4. Robust Audit Logging: Secure digital signatures in distributed ledgers
to satisfy FAA Part 121 compliance verification post-recovery.
Accelerates operational recovery while preserving absolute aviation safety.
